_meta.how_to_regress: npm run check:golden focus-pocus  (dev backend up)
_meta.note: Rewritten 2026-08-26 as a bounded-session tool. The v1 sample is gone with the v1 tool: escalating alarms, snooze counts, break plans and /patterns no longer exist. Two routes now — POST /api/focus-pocus for the three actions that call the model (prepare, stuck, review) and POST /api/focus-pocus/session for timer state, which sits in the AUTOMATIC rate-limit bucket because the default 12/minute would kill a session that syncs. Sessions are held in memory with a 6h TTL and rehydrate from the client copy after a deploy, so a restart between capture and check is normal and not a regression. The start case is byte-stable; the three model cases vary and are read, not asserted. 2026-08-26: prepare now returns stoppingPoint + firstStep + doneWhen + wasVague (was a single target). Sessions carry firstStep, doneWhen and extensionPromises. extend requires a promise of at least 5 characters and 400s without one. stuck takes a blocker (next|missing|bigger|focus). 2026-08-26 (2): doneWhen must operationalise stoppingPoint exactly — same scope, no widening "or". finish-early sets earlyExit true and gets its own screen; time-up does not. The review asks where you LEFT OFF, and the breadcrumb starts from that rather than repeating the first step.

output.stoppingPoint: Gather all the tax documents you have and sort them into a single pile organized by category (income, deductions, receipts, statements).
output.firstStep: Find where your tax documents are and pull them all together in one place.
output.doneWhen: You have one organized pile with documents grouped by category and nothing unsorted left out.

input.target: Gather what you already have and list what is missing
input.doneWhen: Everything is in one place and the missing list exists

output.target: Gather what you already have and list what is missing
output.doneWhen: Everything is in one place and the missing list exists
